summary:
NASA’s SPHEREx space observatory maps over 1 billion celestial objects across 102 near-infrared bands every six months. Sifting through this petabyte-scale stream to uncover elusive near-Earth asteroids, ultra-cool brown dwarfs, and hypothetical outer solar system bodies like Planet X is a massive challenge for automated pipelines alone.

To solve this, Team RIP developed SPHEREx Hunter—a high-performance, web-based time-domain astronomical observatory. SPHEREx Hunter enables researchers and citizen scientists to enter any sky coordinates and stream sub-pixel WCS-aligned multi-epoch cutouts spanning 26 years (2MASS→WISE→ SPHEREx). It features a digital Clyde Tombaugh blink comparator, a mathematically rigorous ZOGY difference-imaging engine (𝐼2−𝐼1) that subtracts static stars into neutral gray while isolating moving dipoles, and an on-the-fly 102-band infrared spectroscopy analyzer (0.75−5.0𝜇m)  resolving atmospheric H2O,𝐶𝐻4 and CO2. By democratizing discovery through one-click shareable deep links, SPHEREx Hunter ensures no moving world in SPHEREx's survey goes unnoticed.
details:
SPHEREx Hunter: Project Details

1. WHAT DOES IT DO OR HOW DOES IT WORK?

SPHEREx Hunter is a web-based astronomical observatory and citizen-science discovery engine that enables anyone to search for moving asteroids, ultra-cool brown dwarfs, and hypothetical outer solar system bodies (like Planet X) in NASA SPHEREx survey data.

The platform operates through four integrated stages:

- Multi-Epoch Astrometric Alignment: When users input celestial coordinates (RA/Dec) or choose a benchmark target, the backend queries NASA IRSA, CDS Strasbourg, and ESA Gaia DR3. It reprojects historical FITS cutouts across 26 years (1999 2MASS, 2010/2020 unWISE, and 2025 SPHEREx) onto a common tangent plane using standard Gnomonic (TAN) WCS transformations, achieving sub-pixel registration across heterogeneous detector resolutions.

- Digital Clyde Tombaugh Blink Engine: A hardware-accelerated 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas rapidly alternates between multi-epoch frames at adjustable speeds (50 ms to 2 s). By leveraging the human brain's motion reflexes, millions of static background stars freeze while moving worlds visibly leap across the screen.

- ZOGY Difference Imaging: Implements the mathematically optimal Zackay, Ofek, & Gal-Yam (ZOGY 2016) algorithm. Background stars cleanly subtract to flat neutral gray, isolating moving objects and transients as high-contrast white-and-black dipole pairs (>650 SNR).

- 102-Band Infrared Spectroscopy: Measures and plots the full Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) across all six SPHEREx detector arrays (0.75 - 5.00 microns). Dynamic array co-addition boosts signal-to-noise ratio by >4x, overlaying diagnostic absorption markers for atmospheric water vapor (1.40 um), water ice (3.05 um), methane CH4 (3.30 um), and carbon dioxide CO2 (4.27 um).

2. WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

- Zero-Installation Barrier: Runs entirely in modern web browsers on standard laptops, tablets, or phones without requiring IRAF, DS9, or Python environments.

- 26-Year Time Baseline: Comparing 1999 2MASS, 2010 WISE, and 2025 SPHEREx turns glacial 0.1"/yr motion into clear multi-pixel jumps.

- False-Positive Reduction: Pairs automated ESA Gaia DR3 star masking with human visual verification to eliminate false alarms from diffraction spikes and bad pixels.

- Instant Atmospheric Classification: The 102-band spectrophotometer immediately identifies whether a moving target is a normal star, an icy asteroid, or a freezing substellar Y-dwarf (T < 300 K).

3. WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT OF THE PROJECT?

The project democratizes petabyte-scale infrared astronomy. With SPHEREx mapping over 1 billion objects every six months, automated pipelines produce too many candidates for professional teams to verify alone. SPHEREx Hunter turns this firehose into an open, collaborative citizen science mission to:

- Accelerate the discovery of cold brown dwarfs and rogue planetary-mass objects near our Solar System.

- Track near-Earth asteroids and Kuiper Belt objects for planetary defense and solar system architecture studies.

- Empirically search for or place strict observational limits on Planet X.

- Provide STEM educators and students worldwide with an accessible gateway to real space mission data.

4. WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, OR SOFTWARE DID YOU USE?

- Backend: Python 3.11+, FastAPI (asynchronous REST API with RFC 7807 error responses), Astropy (WCS coordinate transformations and FITS parsing), Astroquery (TAP queries), NumPy & SciPy (matrix subtraction, PSF convolution, array co-addition), Uvicorn.

- Frontend: Modern JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 Canvas 2D API (sub-pixel rendering and affine transform matrix control), Tailwind CSS (responsive astronomical dark UI), CDS Strasbourg Aladin Lite v3 (HiPS all-sky context), Web Audio API (acoustic target acquisition cues).

- Hardware: Standard consumer laptops (Intel Core i5/i7, 8-16 GB RAM); designed to run efficiently without requiring GPU servers.

5. HOW IS YOUR PROJECT CREATIVE?

- Honoring Clyde Tombaugh: Digitizes the optical blink comparator used to discover Pluto in 1930, enhancing it with modern sub-pixel WCS alignment and multi-epoch animation.

- Dynamic Spectral Co-Addition: Users can interactively co-add spectral arrays via a slider to trade spectral resolution for signal depth (>4x SNR boost), turning complex spectrophotometry into an intuitive hands-on tool.

- Audio-Visual Sonification: Integrates subtle frequency cues via Web Audio API during epoch transitions and auto-detections, creating a multi-sensory discovery platform.

6. WHAT FACTORS DID YOUR TEAM CONSIDER?

- Astrometric Plate Scale Variations: Harmonized disparate survey resolutions (2MASS 2.0"/px, WISE 2.75"/px, SPHEREx 6.2"/px) using rigorous Gnomonic tangent projections to prevent false dipoles.

- Extreme Astronomical Dynamic Range: Implemented real-time arcsinh and zscale contrast stretching with 99.5% percentile clipping to make faint 250 K targets visible without saturating bright field stars.

- Usability for Beginners: Created curated benchmark targets (Barnard's Star, WISE 0855, Epsilon Indi B), an interactive Mission Codex explaining the science, and 1-click candidate flagging with shareable deep links.

- Performance & Bandwidth: Implemented client-side canvas caching and dynamic Level-of-Detail (LOD) streaming so users with standard internet connections experience zero lag.
